pr_body:
The IME was intentionally disabled 8 years ago because it was "not useful for key-bindings". It also broke Alt+Shift language switching. 
Now that text input is an official part of mpv it's time to re-enable it.

Reverts https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/commit/bf6b981367e45c3f926d3e667bba3f3ed6e9dc37.
Fixes https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/9168.
Fixes https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/9168#issuecomment-1748674241.

I can confirm that this has fixed https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/9168#issuecomment-1748674241. Thank you for your efforts.

Edit: This actually doesn't completely fix #9168 , I can reproduce it on Macos. The label of `win` is incorrect and should be replaced with `code`.

There is another issue here, the candidate window for Chinese IME is not close to the input box. This is different from the default behavior of Windows.
![image](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/assets/61936050/8cdc09d3-55de-4a79-99db-dc7be16615f5)

By the way, after mpv initialization, the current behavior of PR will switch the IME to the main IME of the user system (Chinese IME for Chinese users), which will disrupt the use of English key binding (requiring manual switching to English IME). Is it possible to force a switch to English IME after mpv initialization?

>Edit: This actually doesn't completely fix https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/9168 , I can reproduce it on Macos.

IME handling is OS-specific. You should open a new issue for macOS. This PR and that issue only concern Windows. 

>There is another issue here, the candidate window for Chinese IME is not close to the input box.

There is no way to determine where the cursor is since mpv doesn't use standard win32 textinput controls, and there is no way to get that info from console.lua or any other scripts that handle text input since it's private to these scripts.

If I place it on the bottom side of the window, because the cursor position can't be determined, the composition window won't be where the cursor is and will occlude existing console text. If I place it outside of the bottom of the window, the composition window will be out of monitor bounds and invisible if the window is at fullscreen. 

That's why I'm using top left corner as the position for now, to ensure the visibility of the console input and the composition and candidate windows. If you have better suggestions let me know. 

>By the way, after mpv initialization, the current behavior of PR will switch the IME to the main IME of the user system

Can't replicate on Windows 10 and 11. It always keeps the current active language for me. Can you test it in a clean Windows install?

So this should be a feature of Windows platform rather than an issue with mpv. At the same time, I have found a way to deal with the quirks of Windows. For Chinese users of Windows, please refer to:
![image](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/assets/61936050/479c865a-da30-4b72-87d6-4a720dd1d546)
ps: change keyboard layout with win+space.

>So this should be a feature of Windows platform rather than an issue with mpv.

The default IME behavior changed in Windows 8 where the input language became system global rather than per-window. That default can be changed by enabling the "Let me use a different input method for each app window" option (the checked option in your picture). You should uncheck that option if you want the input language system global. 

On all of my test systems it's off for a fresh install, using official Microsoft installation images. Unofficial installation images might have changed that default.

I can confirm that the commit https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/pull/13104/commits/2ac461a6d2d0e137333386c26acdf02a4317f8b7 did not meet the expected results.

I tested and it worked on Windows 10 but not on Windows 11. 

I'm not sure if this is possible on Windows 11. When I called the API to set alphanumeric mode, on Windows 11 the input status on the language bar says it has changed to alphanumeric but it still works like composition mode. Even Microsoft's own terminal (electron-based) has the same problem, defaulting to composition mode. 

MPC-HC and VLC can get away with this because you're locked to alphanumeric input if the focus isn't on a textbox. But because mpv doesn't have this, I think the only correct way to solve this problem is to add the ability for scripts to declare if they're using text input, so that mpv knows when to enable IME.

issue_context.title: Unable to change keyboard language when mpv is open
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

Provide following Information:
- mpv version: 0.33.0-302-g0c9e1e34fd
- Windows Version: Windows 10 1809 64-bit
- Source of the mpv binary: Update 
- If known which version of mpv introduced the problem
- Possible screenshot or video of visual glitches

If you're not using git master or the latest release, update.
Releases are listed here: https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/releases

### Reproduction steps

Try to reproduce your issue with --no-config first. If it isn't reproducible
with --no-config try to first find out which option or script causes your issue.

Describe the reproduction steps as precise as possible. It's very likely that
the bug you experience wasn't reproduced by the developer because the workflow
differs from your own.

1. Open mpv.
2. Press Alt+Shift to change keyboard language.

### Expected behavior

Keyboard language changes.

### Actual behavior

Keyboard language doesn't change. Also if you tab out, change the language (with Alt+Shift) and tab back in, the language changes back to whatever one mpv was opened with.

### Log file

[output.txt](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/files/7075022/output.txt)

The issue will be closed for ignoring the issue template.

### Sample files

Sample files needed to reproduce this issue can be uploaded to https://0x0.st/
or similar sites. (Only needed if the issue cannot be reproduced without it.)
Do not use garbage like "cloud storage", especially not Google Drive.
comments:
There's not an obvious solution.

mpv handles ALT and SHIFT because one could define bindings which include them, so for the language change mpv would need to decide whether mpv or the system should handle this combination depending on other things (for instance, whether or not an actual key was pressed after ALT+SHIFT were pressed and before they were released).

This would require delicate state management which the win32 mpv code tries to avoid.

As it stands, mpv does happen to forward the ALT and/or SHIFT key events to the system (`DefWindowProcW`), however, apparently the system doesn't handle them for reason, possibly because mpv does its own key translation for KB events.

Unless someone knows how to make ALT+SHIFT combo passthrough for cases where other keys were not pressed too, I'd say this is unliklely to be supported.

As a workaround, you could also change the language via the language bar (it's possible to place it at the taskbar).
You can also change keyboard layout with win+space.

Other programs that let you rebind keys (like Firefox, Photoshop) don't seem to suffer from this.

Also this doesn't really address the part where the language auto-switches back to whatever mpv was opened with when tabbing back in. If anything, I think that could be pointing toward the culprit for this:

>apparently the system doesn't handle them for reason

can we have an option to add in input.conf
`shift+ctrl ignore`
that will let this key-combo bypass mpv, and allow keyboard layout change

user will care himself to not have any shortcuts assigned to key-combos that started with `shift+ctrl+...`

> As a workaround, you could also change the language via the language bar (it's possible to place it at the taskbar).
> You can also change keyboard layout with win+space.

Neither of these methods works for Chinese IME.

This is the state when the IME on the taskbar can be switched normally.
![image](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/assets/61936050/de0b16fe-db98-4242-be85-370ca9ce0784)
This is the IME state on the taskbar when mpv is in focus.
![image](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/assets/61936050/65840997-2034-4e47-907b-a54b38b5da01)

It can be seen that when mpv is in focus, the Chinese IME is forcibly disabled and cannot be switched in any way.

Can someone fix the issue of keyboard language switching? This has been bothering me because I am unable to type Chinese characters into the console and other script inputs.

After that, I tested the support of some IME under mpv on Windows: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, German, French.
Then I found out that the IME that cannot be used when mpv is in focus is Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Those other IME can be used normally, which means CJK characters cannot be type in mpv.

I don't know if it's relevant, in mpv.net I added code in reaction to a request from a Russian user:

```
case 0x51: // WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE
        ActivateKeyboardLayout(m.LParam, 0x00000100u /*KLF_SETFORPROCESS*/);
        break;
```

mpv source code don't seem to contain WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE or ActivateKeyboardLayout, at least GitHub code search does not find it.

review_comments: It's not needed because `conversion_mode_init` is only set after the first keypress, which kills the timer now, so this won't be reached.

If `conversion_mode_init` is set for this but the timeout solution fails, it prevents the first keypress fallback from working, so it shouldn't be set. 

> should use the [KillTimer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-killtimer) function to destroy timer after conversion_mode_init has been set?

Added for the first keypress fallback.
